The paper makes a significant and high-value contribution to the graph neural network literature by providing a unified framework that bridges Graph Autoencoders (GAEs) and Graph Contrastive Learning (GCL). The empirical results are solid, with the proposed variants achieving State-of-the-Art (SOTA) performance on key metrics across multiple datasets, and the paper offers valuable practical insights regarding scalability (memory issues with feature-based GAEs) and the role of negative samples.

The weaknesses are fixable (clarifying the protocol, toning down claims, expanding scope) and do not invalidate the main findings.
